## How Carnival Preparations Work

This Carnival tour introduces the theme of each samba school, the ideas behind it, this year’s costume concept and the social themes or issues it addresses. You will see the favelas, the poorer neighborhoods from which the samba schools originated, and learn how Carnival dancers, musicians and costumes are selected, how rehearsals take place throughout the year, what is required for a successful Carnival performance and what privileges come with winning Carnival.

Niterói, often called the “Smiling City,” is a hidden gem just across the bay from Rio de Janeiro, offering stunning coastal views, iconic architecture by Oscar Niemeyer and a welcoming atmosphere where culture, nature and seaside tranquility meet.

Depart Rio de Janeiro from your hotel or designated address for the neighboring city of Niterói, only 15 km away. Along the way, cross the famous Rio–Niterói Bridge for beautiful views of Guanabara Bay and Rio! Historically, Niterói has been considered the second most important city in Rio de Janeiro State and serves as an administrative center. The summit can be reached by car. It is a lovely place for photos, especially in the golden light at sunset.

One of the finest panoramic views in all of Rio de Janeiro State. A quiet, welcoming beach has a long promenade, low-rise buildings and stretches more than 4 km. It is a great place for a walk, coconut water or a caipirinha from a seaside kiosk, especially beautiful at sunset.

## São Pedro Fish Market

São Pedro Fish Market (Mercado São Pedro) is one of the city's symbols, listed among Niterói's seven wonders. Across 36 market stalls, you will find an extensive selection of the freshest fish and seafood, available to buy or sample upstairs in cozy cafés overlooking the bay.

## Oscar Niemeyer Architectural Route

Caminho Niemeyer introduces architectural masterpieces by one of Brazil’s greatest architects:

- Teatro Popular theater.
- Roberto Silveira Memorial.
- Reserva Cultural cultural center.
- The famous Contemporary Art Museum (MAC), with admission included.

## Milton Tavares de Souza Avenue

A panoramic waterfront route with views of Rio and Guanabara Bay. Stops for photos near the beaches and Boa Viagem Island (Ilha da Boa Viagem).

## MAC Contemporary Art Museum

Visit the iconic “flying saucer” building, one of the city’s foremost symbols. The museum grounds offer spectacular views of Rio and the bay. Inside are temporary exhibitions of contemporary art, each offering new perspectives on culture and creativity. Admission is included.

## Icaraí Beach

Walk along the Icaraí Beach promenade (Praia de Icaraí), enjoying beautiful views of Sugarloaf Mountain (Pão de Açúcar) and the MAC museum building. The atmosphere is relaxed and seaside-oriented, with plenty of opportunities for photographs.

## Santa Cruz da Barra Fortress

Tour one of Brazil's oldest military fortresses, built in the sixteenth century at the entrance to Guanabara Bay. At Santa Cruz da Barra Fortress (Fortaleza de Santa Cruz da Barra), you will find magnificent views, historic casemates and watchtowers.

## Lunch at Bicho Papão Seafood Restaurant

Stop at one of Niterói’s best restaurants, serving refined local specialties:

- A small pot of crayfish.
- Shrimp pastries and fried calamari.
- Shrimp with garlic butter.
- Freshly grilled fish.
- Traditional caldeirada, a rich soup of mixed seafood cooked in a cast-iron pot.

You can also try coffee or local cachaça.

## Optional Visits

Parque da Cidade city park and Piratininga Beach (Praia de Piratininga) are available on request. Additional visits are charged separately.

## Price

Duration: 5–6 hours. Price: $284.

## Tour Highlights

Visit artisan workshops using natural totora fiber, walk to Peguche Waterfall, explore Cotacachi, one of Ecuador’s “Magical Towns,” and see Otavalo and its famous Indigenous market, one of the largest in South America. This is a wonderful place to discover Quechua traditions and find authentic souvenirs.

## Artisan Workshops and Peguche Waterfall

Imbabura Province was designated a UNESCO Global Geopark in 2019 for its geological and natural heritage alongside the cultural heritage of its Indigenous communities. Today we visit several communities to meet local artisans and see one of their natural landmarks.

A local guide joins us and leads us through workshops where sheep and alpaca wool is worked. We visit an Indigenous family in San Rafael to see traditional crafts using a natural fiber called totora. Then we visit a musical instrument workshop and enjoy a short walk to Peguche Waterfall.

## Cotacachi and Cuicocha Lagoon

Afterward, we head to Cotacachi for lunch and sightseeing. Cotacachi was selected as one of Ecuador’s so-called “Magical Towns” in 2020 and is known for leather goods. Nearby lies Cuicocha Lagoon, inside the crater of Cotacachi Volcano. We will walk a section of the trail around the lagoon and admire the scenery, especially its two small islands.

Cotacachi is a quiet town renowned for finely crafted leather goods. Workshops produce leather bags, jackets and accessories. You can buy stylish items and also see how they are made by hand. Bright colors, handwoven rugs and jewelry made by local artisans complete the picture.

## Catching Your First Atlantic Wave

Would you like to ride your first Atlantic wave? An exciting experience awaits during a surfing lesson on the famous Arpoador Beach (Ipanema), one of Rio’s iconic surfing locations. The beach offers wonderful views of Ipanema and Leblon and the Two Brothers mountains.

Surfing lessons are also suitable for beginners. English-speaking instructors (with Russian-language assistance on request) explain the necessary surfing skills on shore before you practice in the ocean. The required equipment, a surfboard, is included in the price. The Atlantic awaits its next wave riders!
